h: A man who cannot make new memories hunts his wife's killer in a story told backwards, so you share his confusion scene by scene.

like.t: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
like.r: Another film that treats memory as an unreliable tool, but warm and heartbroken where this one is cold and procedural.
A noir puzzle whose pieces refuse to line up, with more dream logic and far less hand-holding.
The classic hardboiled maze of half-truths that Memento's detective-in-the-dark mood descends from.

h: A betrayed Roman general is sold into the arena and fights his way back toward the emperor who ruined him; big, brooding sword-and-sandal spectacle.

like.r: The original wronged-man-in-Rome epic, with a chariot race that Gladiator's arena fights are chasing.
Another bloody, sentimental crusade of one man against a tyrant, with battlefields shot on the same grand scale.
A slave-turned-fighter leads a rebellion against Rome; more political and talky, with the same noble last stands.

h: A fifteen-year-old writer is sent on tour with a rising rock band in 1973 and learns what the music business does to the people he adores.

like.r: Another loose, jukebox-powered slice of 1970s youth, hangout-driven where this one has a tour and a deadline.
A 1970s subculture seen through a young newcomer who finds a surrogate family, wilder and more tragic.
The same backstage world played as pure parody, a funnier look at the egos and van rides of a touring band.

h: Four Brooklyn dreamers spiral through different addictions in cut-up, pounding montage; a film people admire once and rarely rewatch.

like.r: Another addiction film in hyperkinetic style, but with gallows humor and an escape route the American film refuses to offer.
The same director's descent into obsession, with ballet taking the place of drugs and horror taking over the style.
The foul, funny Edinburgh novel behind the film, written in dialect that makes addiction feel like a daily job.

h: Three escaped convicts bumble across Depression-era Mississippi on a loose Odyssey, with a bluegrass soundtrack doing half the storytelling.

like.r: The Coens' earlier screwball chase with the same pratfalls and tall-tale voices, set in a modern Southwest.
The Depression-era road comedy that O Brother borrows its title and its tender view of the poor from.
More Coen shaggy-dog plotting and endlessly quotable dialogue, moved to 1990s Los Angeles.

h: A record-store owner talks to the camera while he revisits his top five breakups; a rom-com for people who rank things when they are sad.

like.r: The London-set novel with the same list-making narrator, a little more bitter and just as funny about music.
The original neurotic man analyzing his failed relationships and talking straight to the audience.
A soundtrack-driven story of a drifting young man learning to feel again, sweeter and less sharp-tongued.

h: A stolen diamond, an illegal boxing ring and a dozen mumbling crooks collide in a whirl of whip-cuts and cockney patter.

like.t: Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels
like.r: The earlier, rougher version of the same London gangster farce, with a card game that goes wrong.
Crooks who talk about nothing between bursts of violence, only with a more tangled structure and an American drawl.
Another loud, fast British ensemble of lowlifes with a punchy soundtrack, aimed at grit more than at plot.

h: A Wall Street yuppie obsesses over business cards and murder with equal calm in a razor-edged satire of 1980s vanity.

like.r: The infamous source novel, far more graphic and more relentless about brand names and numbness.
Another satire of consumer masculinity with an unreliable narrator, angrier and more openly rebellious.
A lonely New Yorker's loathing of the city curdles into violence, played as sincere tragedy rather than as comedy.

h: Interwoven stories of a drug czar, a Mexican cop and a dealer's wife, each shot in its own color grade to show how the trade touches everyone.

like.r: Another sprawling, many-threaded look at a global industry, this time oil, with the same weary realism.
A ground-level view of the drug economy, more kinetic and more brutal, told from inside a Rio slum.
The border drug war as a nightmare of moral compromise, narrower in focus and much more tense.

h: A FedEx systems man survives a plane crash and spends years on an empty island with only a volleyball to talk to.

like.r: The original castaway story, practical and pious, spent on how one man rebuilds civilization from a wreck.
Wordless survival at sea with one actor, even more stripped down and less sentimental.
A shipwreck survivor on the ocean turns his ordeal into a parable about faith, stranger and more fantastical.

h: A foul-mouthed single mother with no law degree digs into a utility's poisoned water; crowd-pleasing, funny and sharp.

like.r: Another working woman who takes on a powerful employer with nothing but nerve, set in a Southern textile mill.
A true-life whistleblower fight against a corporation, graver and slower, with less humor.
The same corporate poison scandal from the legal fixer's side, colder and more ambiguous.

h: A stalled novelist-professor spends a chaotic campus weekend with a dead dog, a stolen jacket and a talented, troubled student.

like.r: The warm, digressive source novel, with more room for the literary-world jokes the film trims.
Another comedy about gifted, damaged people and a failing patriarch, with more pastel design and less grit.
A sad-sack writer on a road trip full of wine, regret and small flickers of hope.

h: A freshly paroled thief gathers a crew of specialists to rob three Las Vegas casinos at once, all in cool jazz-lounge style.

like.r: The classic con caper with its own charming leads and a plan that unfolds in front of you.
The same crew-and-score structure played deadly serious, with a long cat-and-mouse between cop and thief.
A slick, flirty thief and a sharp investigator trade moves in a glamorous, light-hearted heist.

t: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring
h: A hobbit leaves the Shire with a cursed ring and eight companions in the film that made Middle-earth feel real on screen.

like.r: The lighter, funnier prelude that started Middle-earth, a single adventure with the same sense of wonder.
A fellowship of misfits and an old wizard-mentor against a dark empire, in space rather than in the woods.
Epic fantasy grown up, with a cast far larger and morals far muddier than Tolkien's quest.

t: The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers
h: The fellowship splits in three; the Helm's Deep siege at its core is the benchmark for fantasy battles.

like.r: The full novel behind the films, with songs, history and slower pacing that make Middle-earth deeper still.
Another outnumbered stand against a larger army, with muddier battles and an openly romantic view of heroism.
The ancestor of every defend-the-village siege, quieter and more human in how it builds up its fighters.

t: The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King
h: The war for Middle-earth reaches Minas Tirith while two small hobbits trudge toward Mount Doom; a very long, very moving farewell.

like.r: Another sweeping, sincere epic of faith and sacrifice, with set pieces that still hold up.
A different grand saga of prophecy and war, drier and more political, about how heroes are made by their followers.
Large-scale battles and a loyal hero fighting for his dead, in a grounded Roman setting without magic.

h: An amnesiac woman and a hopeful actress search Hollywood for a stranger's identity, until the film folds back on itself.

like.r: Small-town surface hiding a rotten core, with the same dream logic and sinister jazz.
The classic noir about Hollywood chewing up its dreamers, narrated and linear where Lynch is neither.
A man haunted by a woman who might not exist, with the same doubling of identity and romantic dread.

h: A troubled teenager sleepwalks through 1988 suburbia, guided by a six-foot rabbit that says the world will end in 28 days.

like.r: A time-travel puzzle made on a shoestring, drier and denser, aimed at your head rather than your mood.
A dreamlike, darkly comic fantasy about a man crushed by the system, with the same cult-favorite weirdness.

like.t: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
like.r: Another surreal, melancholy story that bends reality around a young person's pain, warmer and less ominous.

h: Three former child prodigies and their disgraced father reunite in a storybook Manhattan house; deadpan, handsome and sneakily sad.

like.r: The earlier Anderson comedy about a gifted oddball in love with the wrong woman, smaller and quicker.
A deadpan oddball romance that mixes death-obsessed humor with great tenderness, the ancestor of Anderson's tone.
The Glass family of precocious, wounded siblings who Anderson's Tenenbaums clearly descend from.

h: A brilliant mathematician's grip on reality slips as the Cold War closes in; a polished and tear-ready prestige biopic.

like.r: Another math genius who has to learn to live, in a funnier and more working-class story.
The biography the film is drawn from, with the real, much messier life and the economics behind the prize.
A mathematician's obsession with pattern pushed to paranoia, in lo-fi black and white and with far less comfort.

h: A poor poet falls for a dying courtesan in a Paris of mashed-up pop songs, whirling cameras and unashamed melodrama.

like.r: The same director's earlier loud, glittering take on doomed young love, with Shakespeare's words kept intact.
A cynical, razzle-dazzle stage musical turned into sleek cinema, sharper and less sentimental.
A decadent nightclub musical with real darkness underneath the sequins, much bleaker about where it ends up.

h: A raid in Mogadishu goes wrong and the film becomes a two-hour firefight; unrelenting, chaotic and light on character.

like.r: The reported book behind the film, with far more on the soldiers and Somalis who were there.
Another film that puts you in the chaos of combat, with an older war and a more sentimental frame.
A modern-war thriller of constant tension, concentrated on one bomb-disposal man rather than a whole unit.

h: A rookie narcotics cop spends one day with a charismatic, dangerously corrupt veteran in the streets of South Central Los Angeles.

like.r: The honest cop in a rotten department, told with the opposite sympathy and a lonelier ending.
Another Los Angeles crime epic with men on both sides of the law, larger and more operatic.
Same screenwriter's patrol-car view of the LAPD, found-footage rawness and a friendship at its heart.

h: Two sarcastic friends fresh out of high school drift apart after one of them befriends a lonely record collector.

like.r: The comic the film adapts, quieter and sharper, drawn in flat colors that make the boredom hit harder.
The original drifting-after-school comedy, with the same deadpan alienation and a famous odd romance.
Another sharp-tongued teenage girl at odds with her suburb, sweeter and more commercial.

h: A sorority queen follows her ex to Harvard Law and proves that pink and brains are not opposites; a comfort-food comedy.

like.r: Another bubbly, quotable story of a fashion-minded girl who is much smarter than she looks.
Same teen-comedy energy about status and style, with sharper claws and a meaner social order.
A woman and her wardrobe in a tough workplace, with a more cynical look at what ambition costs.

h: In a Washington where murders are stopped before they happen, a pre-crime cop is named as the next killer and runs.

like.r: The other great sci-fi noir about a lawman hunting through a neon future, moodier and with less chase.

like.t: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?
like.r: Same author as the source story, in a stranger, sadder novel that questions what makes a person real.
Another near-future world where the state decides your fate in advance, quieter and more intimate.

h: A teenage con artist poses as a pilot, doctor and lawyer while an FBI agent follows him; breezy, jazzy and sadder than it looks.

like.r: Another charming imposter who invents himself, in a much darker, more menacing tale.
A slick, period con caper with the same love of the long game and stylish wardrobe.
Another glossy crime comedy where the fun is in watching clever people at work.

h: An Irish immigrant returns to the Five Points of the 1860s to avenge his father, only to be drawn to the gang boss who killed him.

like.t: Once Upon a Time in America
like.r: Another long, bruising immigrant gangster saga across decades in New York, more dreamlike and mournful.
The standard for the criminal family epic, with more restraint and less sprawl.
The lurid 1928 history that inspired the film, full of real streets, brawls and nicknames.

h: A screenwriter fails to adapt an unfilmable book about orchids and ends up writing his own panic into the script.

like.r: The earlier Kaufman-written fantasy of a portal into someone's head, odder and more openly absurd.
The nonfiction book the film cannot adapt, a gorgeous profile of a Florida orchid poacher.
Kaufman's directorial debut pushes the self-doubt of a writer much further, into a sad and enormous puzzle.

h: A rage-prone novelty-toilet-plunger salesman stumbles into love and a phone-sex scam in an anxious, candy-colored romance.

like.r: Another odd little tale of a lonely man in a strange situation, played as a comic fable.
A shy, put-upon office worker falls for a woman in trouble, in a much more classic romantic comedy.

like.t: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
like.r: A romance rendered as an oddball experiment in form, with the same blend of ache and quirk.

h: A Jewish pianist hides in the ruins of the Warsaw Ghetto and beyond; a survival story told with cold, almost journalistic detachment.

like.r: The other defining Holocaust drama, with a wider canvas and a protagonist who acts rather than hides.

like.t: The Diary of a Young Girl
like.r: A first-hand account of hiding in wartime, intimate and ordinary in a way that is hard to forget.
A harrowing, hallucinatory vision of war on the Eastern Front through a boy's eyes.

h: Two killers fight for headlines in Prohibition-era Chicago, with every number staged as a vaudeville fantasy in the heroine's head.

like.r: The Fosse stage tradition behind Chicago, with a harder look at the sleaze behind the glitter.
The choreographer's own surreal, self-lacerating musical about a showman burning himself out.
A similarly breathless musical, in a sweeter, more romantic key and with pop songs.

h: A man pulled from the sea with no memory finds he is a deadly trained agent; the amnesiac-spy thriller that made action leaner.

like.r: The much more baroque Cold War novel the film updates, with more intrigue and a different plot.
The great innocent-man-on-the-run chase, more urbane and playful.
A bruising, back-to-basics spy reboot with the same hard-edged brawls and a more romantic core.

h: A mob enforcer and his young son flee across Depression-era Illinois after a hit goes wrong; a bleak, gorgeous father-son gangster film.

like.r: Another Prohibition-era gangster tale of loyalty and betrayal, more cryptic and darkly funny.
The mob family as tragedy, grander in scale and more political.
A killer tries to leave violence behind and cannot, in a western with the same weight of conscience.

h: A newly retired insurance man drives his RV across the Midwest in search of meaning, and finds mostly his own pettiness.

like.r: Payne's next road trip of sad men, with a lighter touch and a lot more wine.
An old man's absurd trek across the Midwest, filmed in black and white and quieter still.
An aging clerk faces a short life and what it has meant; the same questions, asked with more grave compassion.

h: A shy Queens teenager gets spider powers and learns what they cost; the earnest, comic-book-bright film that kicked off the modern superhero boom.

like.r: The first great serious superhero movie, with the same sincerity and a more mythic hero.
A looser, wittier origin story that launched a whole shared universe.
A darker, more grounded origin story with a brooding hero in place of a chatty teenager.

h: Two jet-lagged strangers, a fading movie star and a neglected newlywed, share sleepless nights in Tokyo; romantic without ever quite being a romance.

like.r: Two strangers wander a city talking through a single night, wordier and more openly hopeful.
A restrained near-affair soaked in longing and period style, with even less said aloud.
The classic of two people who meet and cannot act, buttoned-up where Coppola's pair is adrift.

h: A bride left for dead cuts through her old assassin squad in a mash-up of samurai, kung fu and spaghetti-western homage.

like.r: The kung fu classic Tarantino worships, cleaner and more earnest.
The Japanese revenge film whose blood fountains and chapter titles Kill Bill borrowed.
Swordplay as poetry, with the same flying fighters in a more romantic and serious spirit.

h: A dying father's tall tales have always annoyed his son; the film turns them into a fairy-tale life, all giants and witches and heart.

like.r: The short, lyrical novel in episodes that the film expands, quieter and stranger.
Another sweet, sprawling life told as a series of improbable adventures.
A fairy tale told by a grandfather to his skeptic grandson, funnier and lighter.

h: A murder reunites three men whose boyhood was broken by one afternoon; a Boston tragedy about what grief and suspicion do to old friends.

like.r: The densely plotted Boston novel behind the film, with more neighbors and more rot.
Eastwood's other study of violence and its cost, in the Old West.
Another Lehane adaptation in working-class Boston, with a moral dilemma at its core.

t: Master and Commander: The Far Side of the World
h: A British captain chases a French privateer around Cape Horn in a Napoleonic-era sea story built on detail and on a friendship over violin duets.

like.r: The first of the long novel series the film draws from, with richer jargon, wit and friendship.
Another claustrophobic, realistic view of life aboard a warship, from below the surface.
The sea novel of obsession and the deep, stranger and more philosophical.

h: Ten linked love stories collide in the five weeks before a London Christmas; sugary, star-stuffed and shameless about it.

like.r: Another Curtis-scripted British romance, with a single couple and a quieter, funnier world.
The Curtis film that set the template: a stammering charmer, a posh ensemble and a few hard turns.
A sharper, New York take on how love and friendship tangle, with a classic script.

h: A fired guitarist poses as a substitute teacher and turns a prep-school class into a rock band; loud, silly and surprisingly warm.

like.r: Another band of kids finding themselves through music, with a mixtape heart and a Dublin accent.
A rebel teacher frees a school of buttoned-up boys, with Shakespeare in place of guitars.
A love letter to rock fandom, more nostalgic and less cartoonish.

t: Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl
h: A drunken pirate captain, a blacksmith and a governor's daughter race a cursed crew; a theme-park ride that became a summer classic.

like.r: The model for rollicking serial adventure with a roguish hero and a supernatural twist.
The book that invented the pirate story, cruel and slyly charming in its one-legged villain.
A swashbuckling fairy tale with more irony and dueling wit.

h: A human raised by elves at the North Pole heads to New York to find his father; a sweet fish-out-of-water Christmas comedy.

like.r: Another modern Christmas staple with slapstick and a gooey heart.
The classic New York Christmas fable that asks whether to believe in Santa Claus.
The ultimate Christmas weepie, more melancholic and more serious.

h: A home-schooled girl joins the queen bees of a Chicago high school, then tries to take them down; endlessly quoted and still biting.

like.r: The sunnier, Beverly Hills model of the clique comedy with a similar ear for slang.
The darker ancestor, where the cruelty of the popular crowd turns lethal.
A modern teen comedy with a sharp-tongued heroine and a rumor that runs away with her.

t: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
h: After a messy breakup, a man pays to erase his ex from his memory, then fights to keep her in his head; tender, inventive and sad.

like.r: Another Charlie Kaufman script that folds a writer's neuroses into a comic puzzle.
A gentle sci-fi romance about a lonely man and a voice, equally melancholic and warm.
A neurotic, funny post-mortem of a relationship that is still the standard for romantic hindsight.

h: Nine years after a single night in Vienna, two people get an hour in Paris to find out what they became, in near real time.

like.r: The first night these two spent together, which this film reflects on and rewards.
Another brief connection between two wanderers, in a hushed Tokyo.
The ancestor of every almost-affair, stiffer and more restrained but just as aching.

h: A failed novelist and his engaged best friend take a last-fling wine tour through California; a wry, wounded comedy about disappointment.

like.r: Payne's earlier, nastier comedy of petty ambition in a suburban high school.
Another rueful comedy about a stalled writer who wanders through a messy weekend.
Another road trip of damaged people that is funnier on the surface and more broadly affecting.

t: The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou
h: A washed-up oceanographer in a red knit cap sails after a shark with a ragtag crew and a possible son; Anderson at his most melancholic.

like.r: Anderson's first full flowering of dry wit and storybook design, in a smaller, school-bound story.
The great obsessive voyage after a beast, a thousand times more grim and philosophical.
A deadpan, death-haunted comedy that shares its tender oddity and its folk soundtrack.

h: A cab driver is forced to ferry a hitman through one night of killings across Los Angeles; sleek digital night photography and sparring chat.

like.r: Mann's grander L.A. crime saga with cops and thieves, equally moody and in love with the night.
A different, rawer night cabbie in a decaying city, with far more psychosis.
A quiet driver in neon-lit Los Angeles, even more stylized and more stylized in its violence.

h: A hapless Idaho teenager with moon boots and no social skills helps a friend run for class president; deadpan, flat and strangely sweet.

like.r: Another oddball student with big dreams, wrapped in a more literate, polished style.
A different kind of slacker comedy, set at work, with the same dry and quotable misery.
A family of misfits who stick together, with more heart and a bigger road trip.

h: A slacker shop assistant barely notices the zombie apocalypse and then has to rescue his mum and his ex at the pub.

like.r: Wright and Pegg's second riff on genre, a cop-movie spoof set in a murderous English village.
An American zombie comedy with rules and road trip, flashier and less British.
The grand old monster-movie parody, in black and white with more slapstick.

h: A gruff trainer reluctantly takes on a determined waitress as a boxer; a sports film that turns into something far heavier.

like.r: The underdog boxing drama in its most hopeful form, with a simple fight-for-self-respect story.
Boxing as self-destruction, in glorious black and white, and with an unlikable hero.
Eastwood again as a hard old man who finds an unexpected family, more openly angry.

h: Howard Hughes builds planes and films while his compulsions close in; a lavish biopic with period color and growing dread.

like.r: The original portrait of an American tycoon whose power isolates him.
Another monomaniac builder, harder, colder and far more menacing.
A great Scorsese study of a driven man ruined by his own demons.

h: Peter Parker tries to quit being Spider-Man and a four-armed scientist makes it difficult; the heart-on-sleeve high point of Raimi's trilogy.

like.r: A darker, crime-saga take on the same hero-and-villain question, with a cynical city to protect.
The sincere, big-hearted superhero film Raimi was working in the shadow of.
A quiet, grounded origin tale that treats a superhero as a man with a burden.

t: Anchorman: The Legend of Ron Burgundy
h: A preening 1970s San Diego anchorman faces a female rival and a jazz flute; a pile of non-sequiturs that quotes itself.

like.c: Jim Abrahams, David Zucker & Jerry Zucker
like.r: The gold standard of gag-a-second parody.
A rowdy, anarchic comedy of grown men acting like children, with similar quotes.
Another comedy about a dim, vain man in a shallow industry.

h: Four Londoners swap partners, lies and brutal truths over four years in a conversation-heavy drama about desire as a weapon.

like.r: Nichols's earlier all-night verbal war between couples, even more savage.
A couple's falling in and out of love laid bare, rawer and less talky.

like.t: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
like.r: Another bruised look at modern love, softened with fantasy and hope.

h: A hotel manager shelters over a thousand Tutsi refugees during the 1994 genocide, bargaining with killers and ignoring the world.

like.r: Another true story of a man who uses his connections to shelter the hunted, with a more epic frame.
A journalist's friendship tested in Cambodia's genocide, equally harrowing.
A bigger, more Hollywood treatment of African conflict, with more action.

h: Strangers collide across two days in Los Angeles, each carrying prejudice that goes off at the worst moment; an issue film with its pulse up.

like.r: A far more adventurous ensemble about Los Angeles lives that intersect by chance.
A sharper, angrier film about race in a single city block on a hot day.
A sprawling web of intertwined Los Angeles stories, looser and more observational.

h: Bruce Wayne trains with a mountaintop cult before returning to a corrupt Gotham in a grounded retelling of how the hero was built.

like.r: The gothic, stylized earlier take on the character, more comic-book than crime saga.
Another franchise reboot that strips a fantasy hero down to a gritty, physical origin.
A brighter, more earnest origin story with the same cost-of-power lesson.

h: Two ranch hands share a summer in Wyoming and a lifetime of hidden longing; hushed, windswept and devastating.

like.r: Another period love story of the closet, more elegant and more hopeful.
A delicate, aching story of suppressed love told in three acts across one man's life.
A sun-soaked, bittersweet first love between two men in Italy, with a lush interior voice.

h: A CBS newsman challenges Senator McCarthy on air in 1950s black-and-white; a smoky newsroom drama about when to speak.

like.r: Another procedural of journalists taking on power, with a bigger scandal.
Reporters grind out a story that shakes an institution, in modern and plainspoken style.
A television journalist and a whistleblower face down a corporation, more personal and more thrilling.

h: Israeli agents hunt the planners of the 1972 Olympics massacre, and the mission slowly eats at their consciences.

like.r: A spy story about the toll of secret work, cooler and less action-packed.
A long manhunt told with procedural detail and moral ambiguity.
A cold, methodical hunt of an assassin, driven by process more than by conscience.

h: Elizabeth Bennet spars with proud Mr. Darcy among muddy hems and sweeping countryside in the most windswept of Austen films.

like.r: The original, funnier and sharper than any screen version, with the best narrative irony.
Another Austen adaptation with a wise, heartfelt tone and a witty script by Emma Thompson.
A darker, more gothic romance of an independent heroine and a brooding master.

h: Johnny Cash rises from a hard Arkansas farm to Sun Records stardom while pills and a love for June Carter pull in opposite directions.

like.r: Another country-music biopic with a rural girl's rise and a husband who is a mixed blessing.
A folk singer's failure instead of triumph, a mood piece with great songs.
A looser, funnier tour-bus view of rock culture.

h: Truman Capote befriends the killers of a Kansas family to write his book, and loses himself in the process.

like.r: The landmark true-crime book the film is about, as cold and as masterful as its author.
Another story of a man consumed by a murder case, bigger in scope and more procedural.
An ambitious outsider charms his way into something deadly, more suspenseful.

h: A petty thief mistaken for an actor is dragged into a Hollywood murder by a gay private eye, narrating the whole thing with sarcasm.

like.r: The L.A. detective story that every neo-noir winks at, far more serious.
Shane Black's earlier script about mismatched partners, with a little less jokiness.
The same writer-director's second L.A. buddy detective story, set in the seventies.

h: A shy electronics clerk with a collection of action figures is dragged into dating by his coworkers; crude, improvised and tender.

like.r: Another raunchy Apatow-era comedy with a sweet center, about teenagers rather than about adults.
The earlier gross-out romantic comedy that proved crude jokes and sweetness could coexist.
A later improvised ensemble comedy with the same blend of filthy and heartfelt.

h: Two divorce mediators sneak into strangers' weddings to meet women, until one of them falls for real; raunchy and surprisingly sweet.

like.r: Another bro comedy of grown men acting like frat boys, looser and rowdier.
A crude comedy with the same heart, built on one woman and a lot of bad ideas.
A wedding-based comedy from a female perspective, as dirty and with more friendship.

h: A masked anarchist plots to bring down a fascist Britain while a young woman learns to see through his theatre.

like.r: The grandfather of totalitarian dystopias, bleaker and much less showy.
A violent, stylized near-future Britain with a similar fascination with a charismatic outlaw.
A satirical, absurd dystopia of bureaucracy, with more dark comedy and less heroism.

h: Three pulp tales in a black-and-white city with splashes of color, translated panel for panel from Frank Miller's comics.

like.r: Miller's grim, hard-edged reinvention of Batman, with the same fierce style and tough-guy narration.
Another set of interlocking crime stories, with better chat and a looser structure.
The classic noir of fatal women and doomed schemes whose voice-over Sin City is imitating.

h: A teenage loner investigates the death of his ex in a hardboiled-slang noir transplanted to a Californian high school.

like.r: The source of the clipped, cynical private-eye talk that Brick transplants to a high school.
A small-scale neo-noir about betrayal in a small town, with dark humor.
Another strange, moody film about a troubled teenager in a stylized suburbia.

h: Two Victorian stage magicians destroy each other's lives for one perfect trick, in a story built like a trick itself.

like.r: The novel behind the film, told in rival diaries, stranger and more ambiguous about its secrets.
Another Nolan puzzle about obsession and lies, told in reverse.
A rival magician film of the same year, gentler and more romantic.

h: A rougher, newer James Bond hunts a terrorist banker across a high-stakes poker table and a Venetian palazzo.

like.r: The classic Bond formula of gadgets and wit, lighter and campier than the reboot.
The gritty, physical spy thriller whose style influenced this reboot.
The first Bond novel, leaner and meaner than most of the films.

h: A cop undercover in Boston's Irish mob and a mobster inside the police race to unmask each other; foul-mouthed, fast and merciless.

like.r: The Hong Kong thriller this remakes, leaner and more fatalistic.
Scorsese's definitive mob rise-and-fall, funnier and more swaggering.
Another undercover cop who gets too close to the men he is betraying, more human and sad.

h: In a world where no child has been born for eighteen years, a weary man must smuggle a pregnant woman through a collapsing Britain, in astonishing long takes.

like.r: The quieter, more philosophical novel behind the film, with a different plot and far less action.
Another dark, rain-soaked future where a world-weary man protects something fragile.
A bleaker father-and-child trek through a dying world, written in stripped-down prose.

h: A dysfunctional family crams into a yellow VW van to get their daughter to a child beauty pageant; a road comedy about failing and sticking together.

like.r: The original disastrous family road trip, much cruder and more slapstick.
Another family of gifted failures with deadpan humor, in a more stylized world.
Another indie comedy with a quirky family and a dry heart.

h: A bookish graduate becomes the assistant to a terrifying fashion editor and finds out what the job costs; glossy, quotable and sharp.

like.r: The chatty novel behind the film, with a more bitter assistant and a nastier boss.
Another New York office comedy about a woman proving her worth, with eighties shoulder pads.
A lighter, pinker story of a woman whose style is underestimated.

h: Real-time, documentary-style reconstruction of the hijacked flight on September 11; harrowing, restrained and hard to watch.

like.r: Another real-world operation staged as pure immediate experience, with a bigger body count and much more action.
A procedural about the aftermath, with a sustained sense of dread.
The newsreel-style film about urban terror that influenced this entire approach.

h: A hunted ex-assassin chases the truth through London, Tangier and New York in handheld action that never lets up.

like.r: The paranoid 1970s thriller of an agent hunted by his own side, slower and more talky.
Another back-to-basics spy reboot with brutal fights and real stakes.
The classic chase across a continent, elegant and quippy where this one is raw.

h: A hunter finds drug money in the Texas desert and a relentless killer follows; spare, dry and bleak about the world getting meaner.

like.r: The terse novel the Coens follow almost word for word, with its sheriff's reflections intact.
Another snow-bound Coen crime story with a darker sense of humor.
McCarthy's most extreme western, a hallucinatory epic of violence.

h: An oilman claws his way up in California's boom years, and his contempt for everyone becomes monstrous; unsettling, with an unforgettable score.

like.r: The foundational portrait of a magnate undone by his own appetite.
The muckraking novel that inspired the film, more political and less personal.
Another strange, formal portrait of a damaged man, quieter and more elliptical.

h: A sharp-tongued sixteen-year-old copes with an unplanned pregnancy and a plan to give the baby away; indie-folk, slang and a big heart.

like.r: Another sarcastic teenage outsider, prickly and less cuddly.
Another quirky indie crowd-pleaser about a family under strain.
Another soundtrack-heavy indie about a young person muddling toward adulthood, gentler and less quotable.

h: A young graduate gives away his savings and walks to Alaska; a gorgeous, naive hymn to freedom that you may find romantic or foolish.

like.r: The reported book behind the film, more skeptical and more thorough about the man.
The classic that Chris McCandless idolized: solitude and simple living, with less danger.
Another survival story of a young man alone in the wilderness, more brutal and more compact.

h: A cartoonist, a reporter and a cop lose years to the Zodiac case; a long, meticulous procedural about how obsession eats a life.

like.r: Another film of journalists following a trail of documents, with the same paranoid, patient texture.
Fincher's earlier serial killer film, much more lurid and operatic where Zodiac is all process.
The true-crime benchmark about a murder case's grip on the people who investigate it.

t: The Assassination of Jesse James by the Coward Robert Ford
h: A starstruck young outlaw idolizes Jesse James, then helps to kill him; a hushed, dreamy western about celebrity and envy.

like.r: A western about the lie of the legend, with more traditional pacing and a sharper moral edge.
Another elegiac anti-western, snowy and murmured, about a small man who gets in over his head.
A same-year American epic of a destructive man, as slow, but colder and angrier.

h: A law firm's tired fixer discovers his friend's breakdown exposes a corporate cover-up; a tight, grown-up legal thriller.

like.r: A whistleblower story of corporate pressure, longer and more operatic.
The same environmental scandal told from the crusader's side, much more upbeat.
An associate learns his glossy law firm is rotten, in a bigger and more commercial thriller.

h: A child's lie ruins two lovers in an English country house, and a long war years later tries to make it right; lush, cruel and devastating.

like.r: The novel behind the film, with a more intricate layering of narrators and a final turn that lands harder.
Another lush wartime romance of wounded lovers and sweeping landscape.
A child carrying a message between lovers in an English summer, with a similar cost.

h: Two high-school seniors try to buy booze for a party and spend the night apart; filthy, frantic and secretly a love story about best friends.

like.r: The Apatow-produced comedy that taught audiences to expect filth and tenderness in the same scene.
Another last-night-of-school-year ensemble, mellower and with a better soundtrack.
The ancestor of the raunchy teen sex comedy, goofier and less sentimental.

h: A slacker and a career-minded woman face a one-night-stand pregnancy; a raunchy, long-running rom-com about growing up.

like.r: A teen-pregnancy comedy of the same year, sweeter and more stylized in its dialogue.
The earlier, rowdier Apatow comedy with a similar gentle core.
A later hit from the same school of improvised comedy, written from a woman's point of view.

h: A hotshot London cop is exiled to a sleepy village where accidents keep happening, then the story erupts into a gun-blazing action parody.

like.r: The first of Wright and Pegg's genre spoofs, with zombies in place of cops.
One of the buddy-cop movies Hot Fuzz affectionately imitates, played straight.
Another wise-cracking action mystery that knows its genre by heart.

h: A Dublin street busker and a Czech immigrant write songs together over a few days; a low-budget, handheld musical about almost-love.

like.r: The same director's bigger-hearted take on making music in Dublin, with a teenage band.
Another quiet story of two strangers who connect briefly and deeply.
Two people wander a European city getting to know each other, mostly through talk.

h: Three estranged brothers ride a train across India to reconnect after their father's death, hauling matching luggage and old wounds.

like.r: Anderson's earlier family portrait of gifted, hurt siblings, set in a storybook New York.
Another journey of mismatched relatives stuck together, more broadly comic.
Another film of Westerners adrift in Asia, quieter and less ornate.

h: A Mumbai orphan answers quiz-show questions, each answer drawn from a hard chapter of his life; an energetic crowd-pleaser.

like.r: Another slum childhood told in rapid-fire style, but grimmer and with more violence.
The novel behind the film, which is episodic, more comic and goes in quite different directions.
Boyle's earlier hyperkinetic story of life on the margins, darker and more chaotic.

h: Two Irish hitmen hide out in a fairy-tale Belgian city after a job goes wrong, trading insults and facing their consciences.

like.r: McDonagh's next crime comedy, madder, meta and more scattered.
Killers with funny chats and mixed morals, with a more tangled structure.
Another crime film about bumbling killers in a quaint setting, with a very similar deadpan cruelty.

h: A washed-up pro wrestler, broken by decades of punishment, tries to reconnect with his daughter; a handheld, ragged portrait of a body running out.

like.r: Another battered performer, more operatic and less forgiving of its hero.
The optimistic opposite, an underdog who gets his shot, in a much warmer film.
Aronofsky at his most punishing and stylized, where The Wrestler is plainspoken.

h: A cocky weapons billionaire builds a suit to escape captivity and rethinks his business; the wisecracking start of the big shared-universe era.

like.r: The earlier comic-book origin hit, more earnest and less sardonic.
A moodier billionaire-with-a-mission origin story with far less humor.
The rollicking, joke-cracking adventure whose spirit this film borrows.

h: Batman, a new district attorney and a chaos-loving clown wage a war of nerve over Gotham; a crime epic that happens to feature a bat.

like.r: The urban crime epic Nolan has said he was after, with cops and robbers who mirror each other.
The comic that made superheroes into moral problems, denser and more cynical.
Another dark city and another methodical villain who wants to prove a point.

h: A fired CIA analyst's memoir lands in the hands of two gym employees who think it is a state secret; the Coens at their stupidest on purpose.

like.r: Another Coen tale of idiots in over their heads, with a warmer and darker take on violence.
A looser, more beloved Coen comedy of misunderstandings and quotable fools.
The classic satire of national security by incompetents.

h: A bigoted Korean War veteran grudgingly defends his Hmong neighbors in a fading Detroit; gruff and surprisingly tender.

like.r: Eastwood's earlier reckoning with his own violent persona, in the Old West.
A related late-career film of a gruff old man and a surrogate family, sadder.
The tough-cop persona that Gran Torino looks back on with some regret.

t: The Curious Case of Benjamin Button
h: A man born old and growing younger crosses paths with his one great love; a long, sad, handsome fable about time.

like.r: Another sweeping American life told through improbable events, from the same screenwriter.
Another tall-tale fable of a remarkable life, more whimsical.
A different story of love lost to time by the author whose short story inspired this.

h: A bomb-disposal sergeant in Baghdad seems to crave the danger; a sequence of white-knuckle defusals that studies a war addict.

like.r: Another film of the era with a raw, handheld feel and almost no relief.
The surreal and fevered Vietnam film about men changed by combat.
Bigelow's next film about the war on terror, more procedural.

h: A Jewish cinema owner and a squad of American scalp-hunters plot to burn Nazi leadership in occupied France; talky, tense and gleefully revisionist.

like.r: Tarantino's earlier, more freewheeling mosaic of talk and violence.
The classic men-on-a-suicide-mission war film that this one riffs on.

like.t: Once Upon a Time in the West
like.r: A long, slow, tension-filled opening scene, which Tarantino was imitating, in a western.

h: A corporate downsizer who lives out of airports finds his lonely lifestyle threatened by a young colleague and a woman like him.

like.r: Another slick career man forced to think about what he really wants, more sentimental.
The classic comedy about a lonely corporate man, much more romantic.
A man's emptiness gets examined in a quiet, funny way.

h: A paralyzed marine inhabits an alien body on the lush moon Pandora and sides with the natives; an immersive blockbuster built on visual wonder.

like.r: Cameron's earlier space-marine film, much more claustrophobic and violent.
The soldier-goes-native story that Avatar retells in space.
A bigger, more political saga of a desert world and an outsider who joins its people.

h: Aliens stranded above Johannesburg are herded into a slum, and a bureaucrat sent to evict them starts to change; apartheid allegory with a splatter finale.

like.r: Another film with a handheld, lived-in near future and refugees at the center.
An earlier story of alien immigrants in a human city, played as a buddy cop movie.
A smaller, more reflective sci-fi film from the same year, more intimate.

h: A greeting-card writer revisits his relationship in jumbled order and slowly sees what he missed; a rom-com that warns against rom-coms.

like.r: The classic anatomy of a romance in fragments, more neurotic and verbal.

like.t: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
like.r: Another non-chronological look at a break-up, odder and more sad.
A music-obsessed man revisiting his past loves, with the same self-pity and humor.

h: A lone lunar miner nearing the end of his contract starts finding things wrong with his own life; a small, lonely and thoughtful space mystery.

like.r: The cold, majestic ancestor, with a talking machine that is a menace in a way Moon's is not.
A slow, philosophical story of a man alone in space confronting his own mind.
Another lone space worker with machine companions, sadder and more environmental.

h: Three men wake up in Las Vegas with no memory of the bachelor party and a missing groom; a mystery of escalating bad decisions.

like.r: The same director's earlier bro comedy, looser and with fewer plot twists.
Another R-rated mainstream comedy of men misbehaving around a wedding.
A sweeter, younger story of one chaotic night with friends.
